title: A generator does no I/O
statement: A generator MUST NOT read or write files, use the network or start a process. It MUST work only from the context the compiler gives it.

title: A generator reads no clock, environment or randomness
statement: A generator MUST NOT read the clock, the environment or a source of randomness.

title: A generator's output does not depend on map order
statement: A generator MUST return its files, and write their content, in an order that does not depend on the iteration order of a Go map.

title: The library is not a framework
statement: The runtime library MUST expose functions and types only. It MUST NOT scan, discover or register anything by name, struct tag or init(), and MUST NOT call into a service except through a value the service's own code passed it.

title: No reflection, no unsafe
statement: The runtime library MUST NOT import reflect or unsafe; where encoding needs reflection, it MUST go through the standard library at the service's own call.

title: A breaking change is a new major module
statement: The library's API MUST stay compatible within a major version, checked by apidiff in the common registry's CI, and a breaking change MUST ship as a new major module path.

title: One module, released with the common registry
statement: The runtime library MUST be one Go module with one package per concern, tagged and released with the common registry, so one pin names it.

title: Static code lives here
statement: Code that is the same for every declaration MUST live in the runtime library and MUST NOT be emitted by a generator; code that varies with the declaration MUST be generated and MUST NOT be interpreted by the library at run time.

title: One signed compiler holds every generator
statement: STEGO MUST ship as one signed artifact that contains every generator it can run.

title: The compiler runs no generator code it does not contain
statement: The compiler MUST NOT load, download or execute generator code that its signed artifact does not already contain.

title: An adapter reaches only named origins
statement: An adapter that sends a request MUST send it only to an origin its configuration names, over TLS with an explicit CA bundle and no ambient credential, and MUST refuse a response larger than its stated limit.

title: A pulled artifact is verified before use
statement: An adapter MUST check an artifact it pulls against the digest it asked for, or against the trusted signer the registry's ci-pipeline component names, before any other code reads it, and MUST refuse one that differs or that another identity signed.

title: A GitOps adapter writes files and applies nothing
statement: An adapter for a GitOps tool MUST write declarative files that the tool pulls from git, and MUST NOT call the tool's API, hold its credential or apply a resource to a cluster.
